title: Reds’ Eugenio Suárez and TJ Friedl clear waivers, will join team in Chicago
content:
Cincinnati Reds designated hitter Eugenio Suárez and outfielder TJ Friedl cleared outright waivers Thursday and will still be with the team when it starts its series against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field on Friday.

The fact that the front office was willing to part with two players who have appeared in a combined 1,556 games for the Reds indicates that the team is looking toward the future with a month left in the season.

For the Reds, the advantage of either player getting picked up would have been purely economic — a team that claimed either player would be responsible for the remainder of the money left on their contract, roughly $3 million for Suárez and $700,000 for Friedl. While both players will now remain with the team through the end of the season, their respective tenures in Cincinnati will almost certainly not extend beyond that.

In February, the Reds signed Suárez to a one-year deal worth $15 million, with a $16 million mutual option for 2027 with no buyout. Placing Suárez on waivers indicates the team isn’t planning to exercise the option.

Suárez going unclaimed on waivers provides further evidence that there was little market for him at the trade deadline. Suárez, 35, is hitting .208/.295/.410 with 19 home runs in 103 games after missing nearly a month beginning in late April with an oblique injury.

Friedl signed a one-year deal worth $3.8 million in his first year of arbitration eligibility, but because of the steep dropoff in his production, he is a non-tender candidate entering his second year of arbitration.

After starting the season atop the team’s lineup and in center field, Friedl is hitting just .158/.242/.234 in 76 games. The Reds optioned the 31-year-old to Triple-A Louisville in June, and he is hitting just 1 for 34 since the All-Star break.

The act of putting players on waivers near the end of August is hardly an unusual cost-saving move for teams who are out of the playoff picture, allowing competitive teams to add postseason-eligible players to their roster before the Sept. 1 deadline. The lack of outside interest in either player, especially Suárez, who was a pivotal part of the Seattle Mariners’ run to the ALCS last season, indicates how other clubs view their ability to help a roster at this point.

The Reds are 63-71 after Wednesday’s series finale against the San Francisco Giants, 19.5 games behind the NL Central-leading Milwaukee Brewers and nine games out of wild-card position. Their next 25 games are against teams in playoff position before they end the season with three games against last year’s American League champions, the Toronto Blue Jays.
